question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meiosis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meiosis is called reduction division because it reduces the chromosome number of the daughter cells to half that of the parent cell. (न्यूनकारी विभाजन — अर्धसूत्री विभाजन/मीयोसिस)

 

• It occurs in germ cells (gametes) during sexual reproduction, converting a diploid (2n) cell into four haploid (n) cells.

 

• Meiosis involves two successive divisions — Meiosis I (reductional division, where homologous chromosomes separate) and Meiosis II (equational division, similar to mitosis).

 

• It ensures that when two gametes fuse during fertilisation, the original diploid chromosome number is restored in the zygote, and it also introduces genetic variation through crossing over.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mitosis, by contrast, is an equational division producing two diploid daughter cells identical to the parent cell, used for growth and repair.

 

• Prophase and Telophase are individual stages within both mitosis and meiosis, not divisions themselves.

 

NOTE

 

• Telophase (Option 1): It is the final stage of cell division (mitosis or meiosis), not a division type in itself.

 

• Prophase (Option 3): It is the first stage of cell division where chromatin condenses into chromosomes.

 

• Mitosis (Option 4): It is an equational division that maintains the chromosome number, unlike meiosis which halves it.

question: Which of the following weightlifters won the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year award in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirabai Chanu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist weightlifter from Manipur, won the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year award for 2022, becoming the first athlete to win the award twice (she had also won it in 2021). (सर्वश्रेष्ठ भारतीय खिलाड़ी — मीराबाई चानू)

 

• The BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year award was instituted in 2019 to celebrate the achievements of Indian sportswomen.

 

• Mirabai Chanu competes in the 49 kg category and has won medals at the Olympics, World Championships and Commonwealth Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Past winners of the award include Vinesh Phogat (2020) and P.V. Sindhu (2019, jointly).

 

• Mirabai Chanu also won a gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in the 49 kg category.

 

NOTE

 

• Neelam Setti Laxmi (Option 1): She is a former Indian weightlifter, not the 2022 award winner.

 

• Kunjarani Devi (Option 2): She is a veteran Manipuri weightlifter and multiple World Championship medallist from an earlier generation.

 

• Karnam Malleswari (Option 4): She was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (bronze, 2000 Sydney Olympics, weightlifting), but did not win this 2022 award.

question: Which glacier is the source of river Gori Ganga which is an important tributary of river Kali?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milam Glacier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gori Ganga river originates from the Milam Glacier in the Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand. (मिलम हिमनद — गोरी गंगा नदी का स्रोत)

 

• The Milam Glacier is one of the largest glaciers in the Kumaon Himalayas, located at the base of Trishuli and Hardeol peaks.

 

• The Gori Ganga flows through the Munsyari region and joins the Kali river (also called Sharda river) as an important tributary.

 

• The Kali river forms part of the India-Nepal border and eventually joins the Ghaghara, a tributary of the Ganga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other glaciers in the Kumaon Himalayas include Pindari Glacier (source of Pindar river), Namik Glacier, and Kafni Glacier.

 

• The Milam village, near the glacier's snout, was once a major trading post on the trade route to Tibet.

 

NOTE

 

• Tipra Glacier (Option 1): Located near Kedarnath, it is a source of the Mandakini river system, not the Gori Ganga.

 

• Namik Glacier (Option 3): It is the source of the Ramganga (East) river in Uttarakhand, not the Gori Ganga.

 

• Kafni Glacier (Option 4): It is a tributary glacier feeding the Pindar river system, not the Gori Ganga.

question: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 39 A of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: To secure adequate means of livelihood
option_2: To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 39A of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, directs the State to promote equal justice and provide free legal aid to citizens who cannot afford it due to economic or other disabilities. (अनुच्छेद 39A — समान न्याय और निःशुल्क विधिक सहायता)

 

• It is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) listed under Part IV of the Constitution.

 

• This provision led to the enactment of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, which established the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA).

 

• The objective is to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 39 (not 39A) covers principles like adequate means of livelihood (39(a)), equal pay for equal work (39(d)), and prevention of concentration of wealth (39(c)).

 

• The 42nd Amendment (1976) is also known as the "Mini Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.

 

NOTE

 

• To secure adequate means of livelihood (Option 1): This is covered under Article 39(a), not 39A.

 

• Equal pay for equal work (Option 3): This is covered under Article 39(d), not 39A.

 

• Prevention of concentration of wealth (Option 4): This is covered under Article 39(c), not 39A.

question: Pongal is a festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated over four days in mid-January to thank the Sun God for a good harvest. (पोंगल — तमिलनाडु का फसल उत्सव)

 

• The festival is named after the traditional dish "Pongal" (a sweet rice dish) that is cooked and offered as part of the celebrations.

 

• The four days are: Bhogi Pongal, Surya Pongal (main day, dedicated to the Sun God), Mattu Pongal (honouring cattle), and Kaanum Pongal.

 

• It coincides with the Makar Sankranti festival celebrated across other parts of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equivalent harvest festivals in other states are Makar Sankranti (Maharashtra, Karnataka), Lohri (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), and Uttarayan (Gujarat).

 

• Tamil Nadu also celebrates other important festivals like Chithirai Festival and Tamil New Year (Puthandu).

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Its major harvest-related festival is Nabanna; the main state festival is Durga Puja.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Celebrates Chhath Puja as its major festival, along with Makar Sankranti.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Celebrates Makar Sankranti and Rath Yatra, not Pongal.

question: Which state has the highest sex ratio, as per the 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, Kerala has the highest sex ratio among Indian states at 1,084 females per 1,000 males. (लिंगानुपात — केरल सर्वाधिक)

 

• Kerala has consistently topped the sex ratio charts in India since the earliest censuses, attributed to high literacy, good healthcare, and social indicators.

 

• The national average sex ratio as per the 2011 Census is 943 females per 1,000 males.

 

• Puducherry (a Union Territory, not a state) ranks second with a sex ratio of 1,038.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The state with the lowest sex ratio in the 2011 Census is Haryana, at 879.

 

• Kerala also has the highest literacy rate among Indian states, at around 94% as per the 2011 Census.

 

NOTE

 

• Mizoram (Option 1): Its sex ratio (2011) is 976, lower than Kerala's.

 

• Nagaland (Option 2): Its sex ratio (2011) is 931, below the national average.

 

• Manipur (Option 3): Its sex ratio (2011) is 985, lower than Kerala's.

question: Under which of the following Articles of the Indian constitution "Equality of opportunities include its reasonable classification and provisions for backward class of citizens" is provided?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 16 of the Indian Constitution provides for equality of opportunity in matters of public employment, and permits the State to make reasonable classification and reservation provisions for backward classes of citizens who are not adequately represented in State services. (अनुच्छेद 16 — लोक नियोजन में अवसर की समानता)

 

• Article 16(4) specifically empowers the State to make provisions for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens.

 

• Article 16 falls under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18) enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 14 provides for equality before law and equal protection of laws for all persons.

 

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth, and also allows special provisions for backward classes, women and children.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 18 (Option 2): It deals with the abolition of titles, prohibiting the State from conferring titles other than military or academic distinctions.

 

• Article 17 (Option 3): It provides for the abolition of untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

 

• Article 19 (Option 4): It guarantees six fundamental freedoms, including freedom of speech and expression, assembly, and movement.

question: Who is credited with setting up of Brahmo Sabha, for religious reforms, in 1828, which was later called Brahma Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta in 1828, which was later renamed Brahmo Samaj. (ब्राह्मो सभा — राजा राममोहन राय)

 

• He is often called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" and worked extensively against social evils like Sati, which was formally abolished in 1829 under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck, largely due to his efforts.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj aimed to reform Hindu society by opposing idol worship, caste rigidity, and promoting monotheism based on Vedantic principles.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy also founded institutions like the Hindu College (with David Hare) and published journals like Sambad Kaumudi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Debendranath Tagore later reorganised and revitalised the Brahmo Samaj after Raja Ram Mohan Roy's death.

 

• Keshub Chandra Sen later led a split faction called the Brahmo Samaj of India (1866), separate from the Adi Brahmo Samaj led by Debendranath Tagore.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 1): He was the son of Debendranath Tagore, a Nobel laureate poet, and was associated with the Brahmo Samaj but did not found it.

 

• Keshub Chandra Sen (Option 3): He was a later leader of the Brahmo Samaj movement, not its founder.

 

• Devendra Nath Tagore (Option 4): He revived and reorganised the Brahmo Samaj after 1843 but did not establish the original Brahmo Sabha in 1828.

question: Which physicist is known for discovering that any periodic wave can be represented as an infinite number of weighted sinusoids, i.e., the sum of sine and cosine waves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jean Baptiste Joseph Fourier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jean Baptiste Joseph Fourier, a French mathematician and physicist, showed that any periodic function/wave can be represented as an infinite sum of sine and cosine waves, a result known as the Fourier Series. (फूरियर श्रेणी — जीन बैप्टिस्ट जोसेफ फूरियर)

 

• This concept was developed while he was studying heat conduction, published in his work "Théorie analytique de la chaleur" (The Analytical Theory of Heat, 1822).

 

• The broader mathematical technique derived from this, called the Fourier Transform, is widely used today in signal processing, acoustics, and image processing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fourier is also known for the greenhouse effect, which he first described in 1824 in the context of planetary temperatures.

 

• The unit of thermal conductivity measurement and Fourier's Law of heat conduction are also named after him.

 

NOTE

 

• Louis de Broglie (Option 1): A French physicist known for proposing wave-particle duality of matter (de Broglie wavelength), for which he won the Nobel Prize in 1929.

 

• Joseph-Louis Lagrange (Option 3): An Italian-French mathematician known for Lagrangian mechanics and contributions to calculus of variations.

 

• Ernest Walton (Option 4): An Irish physicist who, along with John Cockcroft, split the atomic nucleus (Cockcroft-Walton experiment), winning the Nobel Prize in Physics, 1951.

question: Which of the following laws represented by the formula T2/R3, compares the orbital period and radius of the orbit of a planet with that of other planets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kepler's Third Law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kepler's Third Law, also called the Law of Periods, states that the square of the orbital period (T²) of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (R³) of its orbit, i.e., T²/R³ = constant for all planets orbiting the Sun. (केप्लर का तीसरा नियम — परिक्रमण काल और कक्षा त्रिज्या)

 

• It was formulated by German astronomer Johannes Kepler and published in his work Harmonices Mundi (1619).

 

• This law allows comparison of orbital periods and orbital radii of different planets, showing planets farther from the Sun take proportionally longer to orbit.

 

• Kepler's three laws together describe planetary motion: the Law of Orbits (elliptical orbits), the Law of Areas (equal areas in equal time), and the Law of Periods (T²/R³).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kepler's laws laid the observational foundation later explained theoretically by Isaac Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.

 

• Kepler derived his laws using the precise astronomical observations of Tycho Brahe.

 

NOTE

 

• Hubble's Law (Option 1): Relates the recessional velocity of galaxies to their distance from Earth, evidence for the expanding universe.

 

• Copernicus's Law (Option 2): Not a formal scientific law; Copernicus is known for proposing the heliocentric model of the solar system.

 

• Bragg's Law (Option 4): Relates to the diffraction of X-rays by crystal lattices, used in X-ray crystallography.

question: Nirmala Paniker was honoured with which of the following awards in the year 2019 for her contribution to Mohiniyattam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nirmala Paniker, a renowned exponent and choreographer of Mohiniyattam, was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2019 for her contribution to the dance form. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार — निर्मला पणिकर, मोहिनीअट्टम)

 

• She is the founder of Natanakairali, a research and training centre for traditional arts based in Irinjalakuda, Kerala.

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of Kerala, characterised by graceful, swaying movements, traditionally performed by women, telling the story of the enchantress Mohini, an avatar of Lord Vishnu.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) is India's highest recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nirmala Paniker is married to G. Venu, a well-known theatre and dance scholar, and together they have contributed significantly to reviving and documenting traditional Kerala performing arts.

 

• The eight recognised classical dances of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 2), Padma Vibhushan (Option 3) and Padma Shri (Option 4): These are civilian awards given by the Government of India; Nirmala Paniker's 2019 honour for Mohiniyattam was specifically the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, not a Padma award.

question: The cropping season between Rabi and Kharif is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zaid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Zaid is the short cropping season that falls between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, typically from March to June, involving irrigation-dependent crops. (जायद फसल — रबी और खरीफ के बीच की फसल)

 

• Common Zaid crops include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and fodder crops like moong and vegetables.

 

• Rabi crops (like wheat, mustard, gram) are sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in spring (March-April).

 

• Kharif crops (like rice, maize, cotton) are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zaid crops require significant irrigation as they are grown in the hot, dry summer months when natural rainfall is minimal.

 

• The cropping seasons of India — Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid — are shaped largely by the monsoon cycle.

 

NOTE

 

• Aman (Option 1): This refers to the main winter rice crop grown in eastern India and Bangladesh, sown during the monsoon and harvested in winter — not a season between Rabi and Kharif.

 

• Boro (Option 2): This is a rice crop grown in the dry (winter-spring) season, mainly in eastern India and Bangladesh, using irrigation — a rice-specific term, not the general inter-season name.

 

• Aus (Option 4): This is an autumn rice crop grown in eastern India, sown in spring/summer and harvested in autumn — also a rice-specific term, not the general term for the Rabi-Kharif gap season.

question: Who among the following personalities is/was NOT an Indian Ghazal singer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimsen Joshi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, not a Ghazal singer. (भीमसेन जोशी — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय गायक)

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008, India's highest civilian honour, for his contribution to Indian classical (khayal) singing.

 

• In contrast, Begum Akhtar, Jagjit Singh, and Chitra Singh are all celebrated for their contributions to Ghazal singing in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jagjit Singh is popularly known as the "Ghazal King" and is credited with popularising Ghazal singing using Western instruments.

 

• Begum Akhtar, known as "Mallika-e-Ghazal" (Queen of Ghazals), was awarded the Padma Bhushan posthumously.

 

NOTE

 

• Begum Akhtar (Option 1): A pioneering Ghazal, Dadra and Thumri singer, honoured as the Queen of Ghazals.

 

• Chitra Singh (Option 2): Wife and singing partner of Jagjit Singh, renowned for her Ghazal duets with him.

 

• Jagjit Singh (Option 4): Widely regarded as the most popular Ghazal singer of modern India.

question: In March 2023, the Central Board of Direct Taxes extended the deadline to link Permanent Account Number (PAN) and Aadhaar from 31st March 2023 to ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30th June 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), in March 2023, extended the deadline for linking PAN with Aadhaar from 31st March 2023 to 30th June 2023. (पैन-आधार लिंकिंग — 30 जून 2023 तक विस्तारित)

 

• Taxpayers who failed to link PAN with Aadhaar by this date faced their PAN becoming inoperative, along with a late fee of ₹1,000 for linking.

 

• The PAN-Aadhaar linking requirement stems from provisions under Section 139AA of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) functions under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, and is the apex body for direct tax administration in India.

 

• PAN-Aadhaar linking can be done online through the Income Tax e-filing portal.

 

NOTE

 

• 30th July 2023 (Option 1), 30th September 2023 (Option 2) and 30th August 2023 (Option 3): These are incorrect dates; the officially notified extended deadline was 30th June 2023.

question: In which of the following years was Muslim League founded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1906.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dacca (Dhaka), under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan, with Aga Khan III as its first president. (मुस्लिम लीग की स्थापना — 1906, ढाका)

 

• It was established to safeguard the political rights and interests of Muslims in British India.

 

• The League initially supported cooperation with the British but later, under leaders like Muhammad Ali Jinnah, became central to the demand for a separate nation, Pakistan, articulated formally in the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian National Congress was founded earlier, in 1885, by A.O. Hume.

 

• The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act) of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a demand pushed by the Muslim League.

 

NOTE

 

• 1907 (Option 1): This year is notable for the Surat Split in the Indian National Congress between Moderates and Extremists, not the founding of the Muslim League.

 

• 1905 (Option 2): This year marks the Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon, a key trigger for the formation of the Muslim League the following year.

 

• 1909 (Option 3): This year saw the Morley-Minto Reforms, not the founding of the Muslim League.

question: According to Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), which state in India is the largest producer of natural gas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), Assam is the largest producer of natural gas among Indian states. (प्राकृतिक गैस उत्पादन — असम अग्रणी राज्य)

 

• Assam's major natural gas and oil fields include Digboi, Naharkatiya, Rudrasagar and Moran, mostly located in the Upper Assam basin.

 

• Assam is also historically significant as the site of Digboi, home to Asia's oldest oil refinery, established in 1901.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Considering offshore fields, the Mumbai High (Bombay High) field off Maharashtra's coast is India's largest single hydrocarbon-producing field.

 

• ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is the dominant public sector company responsible for the majority of India's domestic crude oil and natural gas production.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 1): Has natural gas reserves in the Krishna-Godavari basin but ranks below Assam in production.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Includes offshore production from Mumbai High but ranks below Assam in overall state-wise natural gas output for this period.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Has the Cauvery basin reserves but is not the top producer among Indian states.

question:
While using the income method to compute national income, which of the following is NOT to be included?

A) Income from lottery

B) Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares

C) Income from illegal activities like gambling
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• While computing national income using the income method, only factor incomes earned from current production of goods and services are included; transfer incomes and illegal earnings are excluded. (राष्ट्रीय आय — आय पद्धति में हस्तांतरण आय शामिल नहीं)

 

• A) Income from lottery is a transfer income — it is not earned in exchange for any productive service, so it is excluded from national income.

 

• C) Income from illegal activities like gambling is also excluded, since national income accounts only for legally recognised economic activities that are reported and contribute to the value of goods/services produced.

 

• B) Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares is, however, included in national income, because the brokerage/commission is a payment for a productive service rendered by the broker (even though the shares themselves, being existing financial assets, are not counted).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of transfer incomes excluded from national income include gifts, donations, scholarships, and remittances.

 

• The three methods of calculating national income are the Income Method, Expenditure Method, and Value Added (Product/Output) Method.

 

NOTE

 

• A, B and C (Option 1): Incorrect, since brokerage on sale/purchase of shares (B) is a factor income for a service rendered and should be included.

 

• B and C (Option 2): Incorrect, since it wrongly excludes brokerage (B), which should be included, while missing income from lottery (A), which should be excluded.

 

• A and B (Option 3): Incorrect, since it wrongly excludes brokerage (B), which should be included in national income.

question: Under the new IPL rule in 2023, who among the following Chennai Super King players became the first Impact player in the history of the tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tushar Deshpande.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tushar Deshpande, a fast bowler for Chennai Super Kings (CSK), became the first-ever Impact Player used in IPL history in the opening match of the IPL 2023 season against Gujarat Titans. (इम्पैक्ट प्लेयर नियम — तुषार देशपांडे, CSK)

 

• The Impact Player rule, introduced by the BCCI for the 2023 IPL season, allows teams to bring in a substitute player who can bat, bowl or field, giving each side effectively 12 players in a match.

 

• CSK, the defending champions, used this rule at the very start of the tournament, bringing on Tushar Deshpande as a bowling substitute.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sai Sudharsan of Gujarat Titans was the second Impact Player used in that very same match.

 

• Chennai Super Kings went on to win the IPL 2023 title, defeating Gujarat Titans in the final.

 

NOTE

 

• MS Dhoni (Option 1): CSK's captain in IPL 2023, but he was not the first Impact Player substitute used.

 

• Deepak Chahar (Option 2): A CSK pace bowler, but not the player used as the first Impact Player.

 

• Akash Singh (Option 3): A CSK bowler, but not the one who created this record.

question: Which city is going to host the 2026 winter Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milan-Cortina d'Ampezzo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2026 Winter Olympics are scheduled to be jointly hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo in Italy, marking the country's third time hosting the Winter Olympics. (2026 शीतकालीन ओलंपिक — मिलान-कोर्तिना, इटली)

 

• This will be Italy's first time hosting since the 2006 Turin Winter Olympics.

 

• Cortina d'Ampezzo had earlier hosted the 1956 Winter Olympics, making this the second time it hosts Winter Games events.

 

• The event is officially known as the XXV (25th) Olympic Winter Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Winter Olympics were hosted by Beijing, China — making Beijing the first city to host both Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Olympics.

 

• The 2018 Winter Olympics were hosted by Pyeongchang, South Korea.

 

NOTE

 

• Boston (Option 1): Was briefly considered by the USOC as a bid city for the 2024 Summer Olympics, not selected for the 2026 Winter Olympics.

 

• Beijing (Option 2): Hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics, not 2026.

 

• Pyeongchang (Option 4): Hosted the 2018 Winter Olympics, not 2026.

question: The Fiscal policy achieves the macroeconomic goals by using which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taxes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government revenue collection (taxation) and expenditure to influence a country's economy, so taxes are a key instrument of fiscal policy. (राजकोषीय नीति — कर)

 

• Fiscal policy is formulated and implemented by the Government (Ministry of Finance), aiming at objectives like economic growth, price stability, and full employment through changes in taxation and public spending.

 

• The other instruments of fiscal policy include public expenditure, public debt, and deficit financing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Monetary policy, in contrast, is controlled by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and uses tools like SLR, CRR, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, and Bank Rate to regulate money supply and credit in the economy.

 

• India's fiscal policy is presented annually through the Union Budget.

 

NOTE

 

• SLR (Option 2): Statutory Liquidity Ratio — a monetary policy tool used by the RBI, requiring banks to maintain a certain percentage of assets in liquid form.

 

• CRR (Option 3): Cash Reserve Ratio — a monetary policy tool requiring banks to keep a portion of deposits as reserves with the RBI.

 

• Bank rate (Option 4): The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks — a monetary policy instrument, not fiscal.

question: Which of the following folk dance forms is performed by men in Haryana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gugga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gugga (Gugga dance) is a folk dance of Haryana performed by men, associated with the worship of the folk deity Gugga Pir (Guga Ji), a snake deity revered widely in the region. (गुग्गा नृत्य — हरियाणा, पुरुषों द्वारा)

 

• It is performed during festivals dedicated to Gugga, often accompanied by traditional instruments, with performers narrating tales of the deity's valour.

 

• Haryana has several dance forms performed by men, including Gugga, Loor (performed by women), Dhamal, and Khoria (performed by women).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mardana Jhumar is another Haryanvi dance form performed by men during weddings and festive occasions.

 

• Haryana's folk culture includes the Saang (folk theatre) tradition alongside its various dance forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Khoria (Option 1): A folk dance of Haryana performed by women, often during festive occasions.

 

• Gidda (Option 2): A popular folk dance of Punjab performed by women, not a Haryana dance.

 

• Ghoomar (Option 3): A traditional folk dance of Rajasthan performed by women, not a Haryana dance.

question: Which of these is NOT part of the classification of economic activities carried out in an economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law and order.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Economic activities in any economy are broadly classified into three types: Production, Distribution, and Consumption. (आर्थिक क्रियाएँ — उत्पादन, वितरण, उपभोग)

 

• Production refers to the creation of goods and services using factors of production (land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship).

 

• Distribution refers to how the income generated from production is shared among the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit).

 

• Consumption refers to the use of goods and services to satisfy human wants.

 

• Law and order is a governance/administrative function of the State, not an economic activity in this classification.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Economic activities can also be classified sector-wise into Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors.

 

• Some economists also add Exchange as a fourth linked economic activity, referring to the buying and selling of goods and services.

 

NOTE

 

• Production (Option 1): A core economic activity — the creation of goods and services.

 

• Consumption (Option 2): A core economic activity — the use of goods/services to satisfy wants.

 

• Distribution (Option 3): A core economic activity — the sharing of income among factors of production.

question: Which of these statements is correct?
option_1: The economic wealth of a country does not necessarily depend on the possession of resources.
option_2: Countries endowed with natural resources are naturally the richest countries.
option_3: The national income of a country is the total of all its resources.
option_4: Whether resources are used in generating a flow of output and as a result, income and wealth, is immaterial.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The economic wealth of a country does not necessarily depend on the possession of resources.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mere possession of natural resources does not automatically make a country economically wealthy — wealth depends on how effectively those resources are utilised, converted into productive assets, and used to generate a flow of income and output. (आर्थिक संपन्नता — संसाधनों के उपयोग पर निर्भर, केवल स्वामित्व पर नहीं)

 

• Several resource-rich countries remain economically underdeveloped due to poor utilisation, weak institutions, or lack of technology and capital, while some resource-poor countries (e.g., Japan, Singapore) are highly developed due to efficient use of human capital and technology.

 

• This is a fundamental concept in economics and economic development — economic wealth is generated through the productive use of resources (land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship), not just their existence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The distinction between a country's resource endowment and its economic development is central to development economics — e.g., the "resource curse" phenomenon, where resource-rich nations sometimes experience slower growth.

 

• Human capital, technology, and institutions are often more decisive for economic wealth than raw resource availability.

 

NOTE

 

• Countries endowed with natural resources are naturally the richest countries (Option 2): Incorrect — resource possession alone does not guarantee wealth; effective utilisation matters more.

 

• The national income of a country is the total of all its resources (Option 3): Incorrect — national income is the value of goods and services produced/flow of income generated in a period, not merely the stock of resources.

 

• Whether resources are used in generating a flow of output... is immaterial (Option 4): Incorrect — this is in fact material/crucial, since it is the productive use of resources that creates income and wealth.

question: The Gahadavalas ruled over which region of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanauj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gahadavala dynasty ruled over the region of Kanauj (in present-day Uttar Pradesh) from around the 11th to 12th century CE. (गहड़वाल वंश — कन्नौज)

 

• The dynasty was founded by Chandradeva around 1090 CE, with Kanauj and later Varanasi (Kashi) as important centres of their rule.

 

• The most notable ruler of this dynasty was Jayachandra (Jaichand), who was defeated by Muhammad of Ghor in the Battle of Chandawar (1194 CE), an event significant in the establishment of Muslim rule in northern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gahadavalas were known for their patronage of Sanskrit learning and religious institutions, particularly around Varanasi.

 

• The defeat of Jayachandra is often mentioned alongside Prithviraj Chauhan's defeat at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE), both marking the decline of Rajput power in North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Ajmer (Option 1): Was ruled by the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty, most famously by Prithviraj Chauhan.

 

• Malwa (Option 2): Was ruled by dynasties such as the Paramaras, with Dhar as an important capital.

 

• Patan (Option 4): Was the capital of the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat.

question: Which of these is one of the fall out of the industrial licensing system?
option_1: Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition
option_2: Most licenses were used up by backward states
option_3: Most licenses were for importing goods
option_4: Many small private firms appropriated licenses
solution_text:
The correct answer is Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under India's industrial licensing system ("License Raj"), established under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, a major criticism was that large, established industrial houses often obtained licenses not to set up production, but pre-emptively — to block potential competitors from entering the market. (लाइसेंस राज — बड़े औद्योगिक घराने, प्रतिस्पर्धा रोकने हेतु)

 

• This practice led to licenses being "hoarded" rather than used productively, resulting in underutilisation of licensed capacity and stifled competition in Indian industry.

 

• This was one of the key criticisms that eventually led to India's economic liberalisation reforms of 1991, which dismantled much of the licensing framework.

 

• The industrial licensing policy was originally intended to ensure balanced regional development and prevent monopolistic concentration, but in practice often had the opposite effect for large business houses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991, introduced by the P.V. Narasimha Rao government with Dr. Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister, abolished industrial licensing for most industries except a few strategic and sensitive sectors.

 

• The industrial licensing system is often cited alongside the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act, 1969 as instruments that, ironically, entrenched large business houses rather than curbing them.

 

NOTE

 

• Most licenses were used up by backward states (Option 2): Incorrect — in practice, industrially developed states and regions garnered a disproportionate share of licenses, not backward states.

 

• Most licenses were for importing goods (Option 3): Incorrect — industrial licenses under this system were primarily for setting up or expanding domestic production capacity, not for imports.

 

• Many small private firms appropriated licenses (Option 4): Incorrect — it was predominantly large, established industrial houses, not small firms, that were able to accumulate and appropriate a disproportionate share of licenses.
